:::{#exr-projection-practice}
#### Projecting onto an axis along a diagonal line

[A projection onto $\mathcal{S}$ along $\mathcal{T}$](#def-projection)
keeps the piece of a vector that lies in $\mathcal{S}$
when the vector is split along a [direct sum](#def-direct-sum).
Let $\mathcal{S} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 0)}$, the horizontal axis in $\reals^2$,
let $\mathcal{T} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 1)}$, a diagonal line,
and let $\vecf{y} = (4, 3)$.

Find the [projection of $\vecf{y}$ onto $\mathcal{S}$ along $\mathcal{T}$](#def-projection).

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Split $(4, 3)$ as $(a, 0) + c\,(1, 1)$,
and use the second entry first.

:::
